title: Querying logs with KQL
learningObjective: Write and run Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries in Log Analytics to filter, summarise and visualise monitoring data.
foundation: Log Analytics stores logs in tables (Perf, Heartbeat, Event, Syslog, AzureActivity, AzureDiagnostics, StorageBlobLogs…).
A KQL query starts with a table and pipes (|) the rows through operators, like a production line.
engineer: Core operators: where (filter), project (choose columns), extend (add calculated columns), summarize (aggregate with count(), avg(), max(), percentile() by columns or bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)), order by / sort, take / limit, top, join, render (timechart, barchart).
Time: queries use the time range picker or where TimeGenerated > ago(1h). Use bin() to group by time for charts.

Useful queries: Heartbeat | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where LastSeen < ago(5m) (missing agents); AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue endswith 'DELETE'; Perf | where CounterName == '% Processor Time' | summarize avg(CounterValue) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), Computer | render timechart.
Scope: workspace, or resource context (only that resource's data). Save queries, pin to dashboards or workbooks, and use them in log search alerts.

animation.caption: Query logs with KQL tab: queries run over a sample Perf table.

example.title: Finding the busiest VMs
body: Perf | where CounterName == "% Processor Time" | summarize AvgCPU = avg(CounterValue) by Computer | order by AvgCPU desc | take 5 shows vm-db1 at the top; a timechart by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) shows it rising all morning.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Log Analytics Reader on the workspace (or resource-context read on the resources)
limits: See Azure Monitor / Azure Backup service limits
portal: Monitor > Logs (or the workspace > Logs): choose scope and time range.
Write the query in KQL mode, Run, then Chart or Pin to dashboard.
Save the query to a query pack; create a log search alert from it.
configuration.cli: az monitor log-analytics query -w <workspace-guid> --analytics-query "Perf | where CounterName == '% Processor Time' | summarize avg(CounterValue) by Computer | order by avg_CounterValue desc" -t P1D
configuration.powershell: Invoke-AzOperationalInsightsQuery -WorkspaceId <workspace-guid> -Query "Heartbeat | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where LastSeen < ago(5m)"

lab.objective: Build queries that filter, summarise and order performance data.
steps: Run the default (Heartbeat table) and read the semantic error.
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Time range too short or filters too strict, or data not collected.
troubleshooting.fix: Widen the range; check the table has data (… | take 10).

troubleshooting.cause: Column doesn't exist in that table.
Scanning large tables without a time filter.
troubleshooting.fix: Filter on TimeGenerated first and project only needed columns.

comparisons.difference: KQL reads top-down with pipes: Perf | where … | summarize … instead of SELECT … FROM … GROUP BY.

misconceptions.reality: Only the aggregates and by-columns remain.

architectureDecisions: Save common queries and share them in query packs.
Filter by time and table early for performance and cost.

walkthrough.subtitle: Ask questions of your logs with a few simple Kusto (KQL) commands.

steps.label: Millions of rows
steps.title: Which VM stopped sending heartbeats?
body: The data is in Log Analytics, but scrolling through millions of rows is impossible. KQL asks the question for you.

steps.label: Pipe
steps.title: Start with a table, then pipe
body: A query starts with a table name, then passes rows through steps separated by |. Common tables: Heartbeat, Perf, Event, Syslog, AzureActivity, AzureDiagnostics, StorageBlobLogs.

steps.label: where
steps.title: Filter rows
body: where keeps rows that match: | where Computer == "vm-web1" and | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h). Use contains or has to search text. take 10 shows a few sample rows.

callout.text: Always filter by time first; it makes queries faster and cheaper.

steps.label: summarize
steps.title: Count and group
body: summarize turns rows into totals: | summarize count() by Computer, or | summarize avg(CounterValue) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m). bin() groups time into buckets.

steps.label: Shape
steps.title: Shape the output
body: project chooses columns, extend adds calculated ones, sort by or top 10 by orders rows, and render timechart draws a chart.
Example: Heartbeat | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where LastSeen < ago(15m).

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: KQL
recap: Start with a table, chain with |
summarize count() by ...; bin() for time buckets

handsOn.title: Write KQL against Microsoft's free demo workspace
handsOn.cost: Free. The demo workspace is provided by Microsoft with sample data; nothing is created in your subscription.

steps.do: In the demo, close the queries gallery. Type: Heartbeat | take 10  and select Run.
steps.see: Ten rows with Computer, OSType and TimeGenerated.

steps.do: Run the query in the box.
steps.see: One row per computer with its heartbeat count.
steps.code:
Heartbeat
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| summarize Beats = count() by Computer
| sort by Beats desc

steps.do: Find machines that went quiet. Run the query in the box.
steps.see: Computers whose last heartbeat is older than 15 minutes (maybe none).
steps.code:
Heartbeat
| summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer
| where LastSeen < ago(15m)

steps.do: Chart CPU. Run the query in the box.
steps.see: A line chart of CPU per computer.
steps.code:
Perf
| where TimeGenerated > ago(4h)
| where ObjectName == "Processor" and CounterName == "% Processor Time"
| summarize AvgCPU = avg(CounterValue) by bin(TimeGenerated, 15m), Computer
| render timechart

steps.do: Top 5 events. Run the query in the box.
steps.see: The five most common Windows events.
steps.code:
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize Count = count() by EventID, Source
| top 5 by Count

steps.do: Pick any table on the left, expand it to see its columns, and write your own where + summarize query.

check: You wrote queries with where, summarize, bin, top and render.
